{{nihongo|'''Kawasukune Shrine (Shibukawa)'''|甲波宿禰神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kōzuke Province]].

Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== History ===

Interpreting “Kōha” as “river” and “Sukune” as “straight root,” the shrine name is understood to mean “the main stream of the river.” Because three shrines stood along the {{ill|Agatsuma River|Q1636255|qid=Q1636255}} in places named Hakoshima, Ubajima, and Kawashima—all containing the word “island”—{{ill|Kisao Ozaki|Q21698487|qid=Q21698487}} explains that the river itself was deified<ref>{{Cite book|ja |title=Research on the Jinmyōchō of Kōzuke Province |date=1974-12-10 |year=1974 |publisher=Ozaki-sensei Book Publication Society |pages=210-212 |last=Ozaki |first=Kizao |author-link=Kizao Ozaki |doi=10.11501/12266236}}{{Registration required}}</ref>.

({{ill|1783|Q7745|qid=Q7745}}), the shrine buildings were washed away by mudflows caused by the {{ill|Tenmei eruption|es|Erupción del monte Asama de la era Tenmei|fr|Éruption Tenmei|id|Letusan Gunung The main hall dates to the Tenmei era, and the worship hall is believed—based on a {{ill|Munafuda|ja|棟札|zh|上樑記牌|qid=Q8008834}}—to have been built in {{ill|Kōka|de|Kōka (Ära)|es|Kōka|fa|کوکا (دوره)|fr|Ère Kōka|ja|弘化|ko|고카|pt|Era Koka|ru|Кока (нэнго)|simple|Kōka|sr|Кока (ера)|sv|Kōka (tideräkning)|th|โคกะ|tr|Kōka|zh|弘化|qid=Q1325317}} 2 ({{ill|1845|Q7636|qid=Q7636}}){{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|p=236}}.

During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, a Shugendō temple called Kōmyō-ji existed as the shrine’s {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}}, but it was abolished after the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|pp=237,960-962}}.

=== Cultural Properties ===
=== Shibukawa City Designated Important Tangible Cultural Property ===
* Kawasukune Shrine {{ill|Sangaku|Q2569069|qid=Q2569069}} (designated January 30, Showa 50)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Designated Cultural Properties of Former Shibukawa City Area |website=www.city.shibukawa.lg.jp |access-date=2024-08-20 |language=ja}}</ref> – Measuring 190 cm in width and 80 cm in height, it was dedicated in {{ill|Ansei|Q1327259|qid=Q1327259}} 3 ({{ill|1856|Q7676|qid=Q7676}}) by Chiaki Keietsu, a native of Tsukiji Village, {{ill|Tone District, Gunma|Q1077001|qid=Q1077001}} (present-day {{ill|Katashina, Gunma|Q1203661|qid=Q1203661}}). The sangaku calculates the base length of a right triangle using algebra{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1986|pp=273-274}}.

=== Shibukawa City Designated Important Intangible Cultural Property ===
* Kawashima {{ill|Lion dance|Q713866|qid=Q713866}} (designated October 20, Showa 47) – A ritual performed by the Kawashima Lion Dance Preservation Society to pray for warding off evil, good health, and abundant harvests. It is dedicated at the annual festival of the subordinate Suwa Shrine (early October)<ref name=":0" />. Though believed to have been interrupted by the eruption of Mount Asama in Tenmei 3 (1783), an extant storage box for the lion heads bears the date {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 4 ({{ill|1833|Q7587|qid=Q7587}}), suggesting it was revived around that time. The dance is performed by a single dancer wearing a waist drum, and the lion heads consist of three types: male lion (Hōgan), female lion, and child lion{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1986|pp=299-230}}.
